belongs_to: Sierpinski Carpet: 'It is made by taking a square, breaking it into 9 smaller squares, and then removing the central square (see the figure below)'
description: Three equal magenta (pink-purple) squares in a row on white, followed by '. . .', each captioned underneath: 'Step 0', 'Step 1', 'Step 2'. Step 0: one plain solid magenta square, no lines, no hole. Step 1: the same square cut by faint light lines into a 3 x 3 grid of 9 equal small squares; the centre square is removed (white hole); the other 8 small squares are magenta. So 8 squares remain, 1 hole. Step 2: a 9 x 9 grid of 81 tiny equal squares (faint light grid lines on the magenta parts, grid lines of the 3 x 3 blocks coincide with every third line). The central 3 x 3 block (9 tiny squares) is ONE white square hole (same size as the Step 1 hole). In each of the 8 outer 3 x 3 blocks the centre tiny square is removed, giving 8 small single-cell white holes at (row, column) = (2,2), (2,5), (2,8), (5,2), (5,8), (8,2), (8,5), (8,8) counting rows from the top and columns from the left, 1 to 9. Counts at Step 2: 1 big hole + 8 small holes = 9 holes; magenta tiny squares remaining = 81 - 9 - 8 = 64. The three squares are the same overall size.
unclear: The two light diagonal watermark stripes ('NCERT not to be republished') cross the page and are not part of the figure.

belongs_to: Sierpinski Carpet, top of page 2: a single larger picture captioned 'Sierpinski Carpet' above 'Draw the initial few steps (at least till Step 2) of the shape sequence that leads to the Sierpinski Carpet'
description: One single small magenta square (about 137 x 136 px on the page image) on white, centred, caption 'Sierpinski Carpet', no step label, no grid lines drawn. It is the carpet at a late step: 1 large white square hole in the centre (side = 1/3 of the carpet side); 8 white holes of side 1/9 at the centres of the 8 outer thirds (3 in the top row, 2 in the middle row left and right, 3 in the bottom row); then many holes of side 1/27 (8 around each 1/9-hole, 64 in all) and a fine dotted texture of tiny holes of side 1/81. Same square-hole pattern repeated at 4 sizes, so it looks like Step 4 (hole sizes 1/3, 1/9, 1/27, 1/81 of the side visible).
unclear: Exact step number is not printed; judged as about Step 4 from the visible hole sizes (resolution is low).

belongs_to: Sierpinski Gasket: 'An equilateral triangle is broken up into 4 identical equilateral triangles by joining the midpoints ... then the central triangle is removed'; also the picture answering Figure it Out Q1 'Draw the initial few steps (at least till Step 2)'
description: Three equal equilateral triangles, apex up, magenta (purple-pink) on white, in a row followed by '. . .', captions underneath 'Step 0', 'Step 1', 'Step 2'. Step 0: one solid triangle. Step 1: three solid up-pointing triangles (one at the top, two side by side at the bottom, touching at their corners) with the central inverted triangle white (hole). 3 triangles remain, 1 hole. Step 2: nine small solid up-pointing triangles arranged as three groups of three (a top group, a bottom-left group, a bottom-right group), i.e. rows from the top of 1, 2, 2, 4 small triangles (1 + 2 + 2 + 4 = 9). Holes: the one big central inverted triangle (the Step 1 hole, half the side of the whole) plus 3 small inverted triangles, one in the middle of each group of three = 4 holes. Remaining triangles = 9.
unclear: Row-by-row arrangement of the 9 small triangles (1, 2, 2, 4 from the top) is read from the picture; the 4-row structure is certain.

belongs_to: Koch Snowflake: 'we start with an equilateral triangle. Each side is divided into 3 equal parts and an equilateral triangle is raised over the middle part'; also answers Figure it Out Q1 'Draw the initial few steps (at least till Step 2)'
description: Three green (solid fill, one flat green) shapes in a row followed by '. . .', captions 'Step 0', 'Step 1', 'Step 2'. Step 0: a solid equilateral triangle, apex up, horizontal base. Step 1: a six-pointed star (hexagram): the triangle with a small equilateral triangle raised on the middle third of each of its 3 sides; 6 tips (one pointing straight up, one straight down, two on the left, two on the right), outline of 12 equal sides. Step 2: the 12 sides each carry a new small bump on their middle third, so the outline has 48 sides; the six main star tips each now have two small notches/bumps and the six concave corners between the tips each show a small bump; shape looks like a 12-sided snowflake with small teeth. Overall the shapes grow in size from Step 0 to Step 2 as drawn.
unclear: Side counts (3, 12, 48) are derived from the construction rule, not counted tooth by tooth on the picture.

belongs_to: Koch Snowflake: single large picture captioned 'Koch Snowflake' below the Step 0-2 row
